episodes.171256: An easterly wave was located just south of El Paso, Texas on August 17, 2022. Associated with this wave was an above normal amount of moisture that produced persistent shower activity across southern New Mexico. This stratiform precipitation moved into southern Lincoln County during the early morning hours of August 17th. While this activity was not convective in nature and did not have very high rain rates, it did move over the McBride burn scar and several hours of even light, steady rain produced flash flooding on the burn scar near Ruidoso. Meanwhile, more typical convective activity in northwest New Mexico produced flash flooding at Chaco National Park.
episodes.171885: Morning convection produces waterspouts across the coastal waters near Madeira Beach and Fort Myers.
episodes.171916: A 42-year-old woman was killed, and a 10-year-old girl and 18-year-old woman were injured after lightning struck a tree near to them as they were walking along Park Villa Place in Winter Springs.
episodes.171922: Thunderstorms pushing offshore from the Volusia and Brevard County coasts produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.171991: A cold front brought isolated to scattered severe thunderstorms with large hail to portions of South Central Nebraska on the evening of August 18th. The first signs of thunderstorm development along the cold front showed itself in Valley County between 3 PM to 4 PM CDT. Temperatures ahead of the front were in the 80s, which was supportive of moderate instability. As instability increased ahead of the front between 4 PM and 5 PM, thunderstorms strengthened and became severe on an isolated basis roughly near the Highway 92 corridor. By 5 PM, a storm near Ravenna in far northeast Buffalo County developed supercell characteristics and began to produce significant amounts of large hail, including up to golf ball size. This storm weakened as it moved southeast through eastern Buffalo County by 6 PM, but a new intense storm developed over central Buffalo County and also became severe and produced large hail just northeast and east of Kearney in the Gibbon area. Around the same time, a lone/isolated supercell developed just north of Genoa along the Boone/Platte County line and quickly became severe. This storm slowly moved south into eastern Nance County between 6:00-6:30 PM, and ended up producing the largest hail of the evening, up to baseball size, in and around Genoa. Significant damage occurred as a result, particularly to crops, vehicles, and roofs. The storm weakened as it moved into Polk County, but still managed to produce severe hail up to ping pong ball size in western Polk County between 7-7:30 PM. Activity quickly decreased in coverage and severity as nocturnal cooling set in between 7:30-8 PM.
episodes.172235: A weak area of low surface low pressure formed along a frontal boundary that was draped across the local area. Aloft, shortwave impulses traversed with the better dynamic |forcing over southeast GA. The entire airmass was primed (PWAT over 2 inches) and prevailing westerly steering flow focused the strongest convection along the sea breezes mergers toward the I-95 corridor in the afternoon and into the evening. A cluster of storms formed along the front across NE FL and Duval county. When these slow moving storms encountered the east coast sea breeze as it moved inland, very heavy rainfall rates produced local flooding across portions of downtown Jacksonville, including the Hogans Creek basin near UF Shands.
episodes.172302: A week cold front initiated storms in eastern Nebraska resulting in widespread hail reports with the largest size reported at 2.75.
episodes.172435: Thunderstorms initially developed along and ahead of a weak southeasterly moving cold front over western North Dakota, with a second area of storms developing over south central North Dakota along a staunch outflow boundary. A few of these storms became severe, producing strong wind gusts. The strongest reported wind gust of 61 mph occurred near Watford City in McKenzie County.
episodes.172446: There was an upper level low pressure system over Northern Mexico. A cold front was across the Permian Basin. These features brought an increase in lift across West Texas. High low-level moisture was in place. These conditions resulted in thunderstorms that produced high wind gusts in Brewster County.
episodes.172924: Scattered strong summer storms resulted in gusty winds in excess of 34 knots across portions of the coastal waters.
episodes.173006: A storm system moving eastward across the northern Gulf spread heavy rain northward into the eastern Prince William Sound area resulting in heavy rain for places such as Cordova and Valdez. As a result, numerous rivers and streams water levels rose due to the heavy rain.
episodes.173007: Multiple systems moving through Southcentral with rounds of heavy rain with not much dry time in between them resulted in rivers on the Kenai Peninsula especially the Kenai River remaining at elevated water levels through this time frame.
episodes.173201: Storms in a northwest flow regime moved across northeast South Dakota during the afternoon and produced 1 inch hail.
episodes.173204: A summer cold front helped to ignite thunderstorms primarily along and south of the Interstate 20 corridor on the evening of Wednesday August 17. Damaging wind gusts associated with microbursts accompanied a few of these storms.
episodes.173471: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. A few storms produced damaging wind gusts with impacts to trees and power lines.
episodes.173536: An isolated thunderstorm developed in Cameron Parish producing a landspout while another storm developed in New Iberia causing wind damage.
episodes.173541: Abundant moisture (1.8-2.0) and an unstable environment (MUCAPE 2,000-4,000 J/kg) across south-central and southwest Arizona allowed for convective development to become strong to severe. Thunderstorms initiated over the high terrain of northern Arizona before working toward the south into the lower deserts. Severe thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts upwards of 60-70 mph along with several reports of flash flooding. No injuries were reported.
episodes.173630: A stalled frontal boundary combined plenty of moisture led several rounds of heavy rain which caused flooding in southwest Alabama.
episodes.173632: Devils Lake Basin severe thunderstorm that moved through during the early morning hours on the 18th. We received reports of damaging winds and severe hail.
episodes.173733: Thunderstorms resulted in flash flooding over several days, which included Zion National Park.
episodes.173778: Waterspouts developed along a convective cloud line oceanside of the Lower Florida Keys in weak west-southwest lower tropospheric flow.
episodes.173801: Persistent moist monsoonal flow fueled thunderstorms over northwest Arizona. Several storms produced flash flooding.
episodes.173877: A cold front plowed into an environment with roughly 1500 J/kg MLCAPE but weak shear, which resulted in numerous thunderstorms with brief intense updrafts. The strongest storms produced isolated damaging wind gusts and hail up to golf ball size.  By evening, a stronger low-level flow ahead of the front resulted in a slightly stronger storm with hail up to 2.5 inches in diameter across northwest Iowa.
episodes.173880: A cold front plowed into an environment with roughly 1500 J/kg MLCAPE but weak shear, which resulted in numerous thunderstorms with brief intense updrafts. The strongest storms produced isolated damaging wind gusts and hail up to golf ball size. By evening, a stronger low-level flow ahead of the front resulted in a slightly stronger storm with hail up to 2.5 inches in diameter across northwest Iowa.
episodes.173984: Deep monsoon moisture over northern Arizona brought thunderstorms with heavy rain and flash flooding.
episodes.174063: Very heavy rainfall occurred over Webb and Duval Counties associated with a tropical low pressure system on the 15th and 16th. Flood wave that originated in San Casamiro Creek in Webb County flowed into the Nueces River, Major river flooding occurred from southeast La Salle County through McMullen County to Live Oak County from the 17th through the 24th.
episodes.178463: A line of slow moving showers and thunderstorms developed over portions of northeast Louisiana in the early morning of August 18th. Training of these thunderstorms led to some flooding.
episodes.178907: A line of slow moving showers and thunderstorms developed over portions of Mississippi in the early morning of August 18th. Training of these thunderstorms led to some flooding.

Seminole County Emergency Management and local broadcast media relayed information about a lightning strike that killed a 42-year-old woman, and injured a 10-year-old girl and 18-year-old woman. The incident occurred near the 1300th block of Park Villa Place in Winter Springs at approximately 1320LST. Bystanders reported that lightning struck a tree just as the three victims were walking nearby. First responders and bystanders performed life saving measures, and all three victims were transported to local hospitals. The 42-year-old woman later died from her injuries, while the 10-year-old and 18-year-old were treated for minor injuries and later released.

Around 4 pm, street flooding was first reported along Myrtle Avenue. There was about inches of water in depth across the street. This report was from Broadcast media. At 410 pm, broadcast media reported street flooding along Main Street in the Springfield area of north Jacksonville. There was a video shared via social media that showed about 6 inches of water across the road with water rise tot he clearance height of cars. There was also a video of Hogan's Creek exceeding bank full into the grass and over the sidewalk. At 515 pm, emergency management relayed that there was severe parking lot flooding with vehicles stranded in the parking lot due to Hogans Creek flooding and very poor drainage at UF Shands in the Pavilion parking lot. This is a known drainage issue area. Some flooded water infiltrated into the Pavilion building into the lower floor.  Radar indicated about 2-2.5 inches of rainfall in about 1-1.25 hrs across these areas.  The cost of damage is an estimate, and it is likely an underestimate for the damage caused.

The service hydrologist spoke to Scott Benda, the Valdez Flood Manager, and found out that rivers in the area were high with some low areas taking on water along Lowe River and Glacier Steam.  The Town of Valdez did not experience any high water or low areas of flooding.  Alpine Woods has a fortified dike, which was relined with rocks; the sub-division was not impacted by this event because of the work on the dike.  Overall all streams were high, with ample groundwater.
